topics.title: Coursework
topics.summary: Permission depends on the School and task. HGSE permits learning uses such as clarification and brainstorming, but submitting AI-created assignments as your own is prohibited unless the instructor specifies otherwise. Social Studies has a broader default prohibition covering submitted work and thesis stages, with scoped course alternatives and approved thesis exceptions.
topics.scope: Read the school, course, assessment and audience scope in each quoted claim

claims.text: FAS Office of Undergraduate Education requires faculty to inform students of the policies governing generative AI use in class. It recommends posting the policy on Canvas. This communication requirement does not choose an AI permission policy for the course.

evidence.quote: All faculty are required to inform students of the policies governing generative AI use in class. Whether students in your course are forbidden from using ChatGPT or expected to explore its limits, a policy helps ensure that your expectations for appropriate interaction with generative AI tools are clear to students.

evidence.quote: More specifically, you should post your policy on your Canvas site.

claims.text: HGSE states that, unless the instructor specifies otherwise, using generative AI to create all or part of a course assignment and submit it as one’s own violates its Academic Integrity Policy. Permissible learning uses include clarification, brainstorming and contextual scenarios; students must discuss uncertain uses with the instructor before use.

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise specified by your instructor, it is a violation of the HGSE Academic Integrity Policy to use generative AI to create all or part of an assignment for a course (e.g., a paper, memo, presentation, or short response) and submit it as your own.

claims.text: Social Studies prohibits generative or agentic AI assistance in submitted coursework, exams/quizzes and all thesis stages by default. Instructors may publish alternative syllabus rules but must require disclosure. Thesis exceptions are case-specific: obtain supervisor approval, submit the AI Policy Attestation request, and secure DUS approval by November 1 of senior year, or April 1 for off-cycle fall seniors. The AI Policy Attestation form is required in consultation with the supervisor at Prospectus submission and again in senior year. Thesis work cannot reuse AI-assisted work from another course merely because that course allowed it. These rules apply to Social Studies requirements.

evidence.quote: Policy: the use of generative or agentic AI in any form is prohibited for aid in analyzing, idea-generation, research, formatting, organizing, outlining, drafting, revising, or editing any work submitted in Social Studies courses or other concentration requirements.

evidence.quote: This includes, but is not limited to, papers or responses or posts of any kind or length, in-class presentations, exams and quizzes, preparatory work for the senior thesis (e.g., the Prospectus), research and analysis for the senior thesis, and the drafting, editing, or revising of the senior thesis.
evidence.title: AI Policy | The Committee on Degrees in Social Studies

topics.title: Exams
topics.summary: HLS Graduate Program examination restrictions and Social Studies rules have specific scopes and written exceptions. They are not a single Harvard-wide exam rule.
topics.scope: Read the school, course, assessment and audience scope in each quoted claim

claims.text: The Harvard Law Graduate Program permits AI queries to clarify exam-relevant concepts while studying, but prohibits queries about exam subject matter during the exam. Pre-writing AI text for incorporation into an exam is not permitted. Instructors may set different rules only when described in writing and communicated to all students. This applies to the Graduate Program policy, not all Harvard courses.

evidence.quote: While preparing for an exam, a student would be permitted to email another person about the subject matter of the exam and/or ask that person to explain a relevant concept. Similarly, while studying for an exam, a student would be permitted to submit a prompt to an artificial intelligence application about topics or concepts relevant to the exam. In contrast, a student would not be permitted to ask either another person or an artificial intelligence application to pre-write text for the student and then incorporate that text into their exam.
evidence.title: Graduate Program Handbook — Policies - Harvard Law School | Harvard Law School
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 171-171; exact character range 14460:15007; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: During the administration of an exam, a student would not be permitted to email another person about the subject matter of the exam and/or ask another person to explain a relevant concept. Similarly, during the administration of an exam, a student is not permitted to submit a prompt to an artificial intelligence application about the subject matter of the exam and concepts relevant thereto.
evidence.title: Graduate Program Handbook — Policies - Harvard Law School | Harvard Law School
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 172-172; exact character range 15008:15401; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: An instructor may provide, for their course, rules different from those stated in this policy, as long as the rules are (1) described in writing and (2) communicated to all students in the course (for instance, stated in the course syllabus). topics.title: Privacy & sensitive data
topics.summary: Use approved accounts within data limits. HUIT general tools support at most Level 3; HMS meeting assistants at most Level 2 and separately requested research tools may support Level 4. Consent and DUA limits still apply.
topics.scope: Read the school, course, assessment and audience scope in each quoted claim

claims.text: Harvard guidance says Level 2 and above confidential data should not be entered into publicly available generative AI tools and must only be entered into tools assessed and approved for that use. HUIT-listed managed general-use tools are approved up to Level 3 with a Harvard account and are not approved for Level 4. Separate HMS Level 4 research/development services require their own access and data-use conditions.

evidence.quote: You should not enter data classified as confidential (Level 2 and above, including non-public research data, finance, HR, student records, medical information, etc.) into publicly-available generative AI tools, in accordance with the University’s Information Security Policy . Information shared with generative AI tools using default settings is not private and could expose proprietary or sensitive information to unauthorized parties.
evidence.title: Generative AI Guidelines | Harvard University Information Technology
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 49-49; exact character range 1239:1676; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: Level 2 and above confidential data must only be entered into generative AI tools that have been assessed and approved for such use by Harvard’s Information Security and Data Privacy office. See below for more information about approved tools.

claims.text: Harvard meeting guidance says AI assistants should not be used except approved tools with contractual protections or applicable approved pilots/accommodations. Participants must be informed and all must consent before recording/transcription begins. The guidance says not to use assistants when participants object (with a disability-accommodation consultation route), and to disable them in meetings involving Level 3 or higher information. Summaries must be reviewed before limited sharing; retention and litigation holds also apply.

claims.text: Social Studies prohibits generative or agentic AI assistance in submitted coursework, exams/quizzes and all thesis stages by default. Instructors may publish alternative syllabus rules but must require disclosure. Thesis exceptions are case-specific: obtain supervisor approval, submit the AI Policy Attestation request, and secure DUS approval by November 1 of senior year, or April 1 for off-cycle fall seniors. The AI Policy Attestation form is required in consultation with the supervisor at Prospectus submission and again in senior year. Thesis work cannot reuse AI-assisted work from another course merely because that course allowed it. These rules apply to Social Studies requirements.

evidence.quote: Policy: the use of generative or agentic AI in any form is prohibited for aid in analyzing, idea-generation, research, formatting, organizing, outlining, drafting, revising, or editing any work submitted in Social Studies courses or other concentration requirements.
